questions.topic: Index Rebuild-and-Swap with Versioned Aliases
questions.question: What is rebuild-and-swap?
options: Patch the serving index in place during low traffic
Build a new index beside the old, validate, move the alias
Rebuild the index on the machines that already serve it
Copy the old index under a new name and keep both of them live

questions.topic: Index Rebuild-and-Swap with Versioned Aliases
questions.question: Why do consumers address only the alias?
options: Aliases let the query planner compress the request
Aliases occupy less metadata storage than index names
Addressing the alias lets the build skip its validation
The swap is one atomic move with no mixed-fleet window

questions.topic: Index Rebuild-and-Swap with Versioned Aliases
questions.question: Where does the new index build read from?
options: From the old index, which is already deduplicated
From the production query logs of the last thirty days
From the answer cache, which holds the served content
From the lake's silver truth, never from another copy

questions.topic: Index Rebuild-and-Swap with Versioned Aliases
questions.question: A build finishes at 23:40 from a 17:00 snapshot. What happens before the swap?
options: The index is published as soon as the build finishes
Ingestion pauses until the alias has finished moving
The events since 17:00 are replayed onto the new index
The 17:00 snapshot is discarded and a fresh one is taken

questions.topic: Index Rebuild-and-Swap with Versioned Aliases
questions.question: Why is the new index exercised with a production-query replay before the alias moves?
options: To collect fresh training data for the next embedding model
So caches and autoscaling are hot before real users arrive
To grow the golden set with queries seen in production
To shrink the index by dropping never-queried postings

questions.topic: Index Rebuild-and-Swap with Versioned Aliases
questions.question: What does a generation tag comprise?
options: The build date and the cloud region it was built in
The embedding model alone, since vectors define the space
Embedding model, chunker version, quantization, and build
The alias name plus the tenant namespaces it covers

questions.topic: Shadow Index Validation Before Cutover
questions.question: What is the correct order of validation gates?
options: Canary soak, shadow traffic, golden set, structural
Golden set, structural, canary soak, shadow traffic
Structural, golden set, shadow traffic, canary soak
Shadow traffic, canary soak, structural, golden set

questions.topic: Shadow Index Validation Before Cutover
questions.question: What does shadow traffic do?
options: Mirrors live queries to the new index without serving them
Routes production traffic to both indexes permanently
Replaces the golden set with randomly sampled queries
Replays yesterday's queries against the old index as a baseline

questions.topic: Shadow Index Validation Before Cutover
questions.question: Which problem is shadow traffic designed to catch that golden sets usually miss?
options: A known adjudicated query regressing on the new index
Schema mismatches between the chunk and vector tables
A model version tag missing from the new generation
Latency behavior and tail queries under the real mix

questions.topic: Shadow Index Validation Before Cutover
questions.question: Top-10 overlap between old and new indexes is 40 percent. What is the right response?
options: Swap immediately, since changed results are the point
Roll the build back at once and start it again from truth
Investigate a sample of changed queries before proceeding
Lower the golden-set thresholds until the overlap passes

questions.topic: Shadow Index Validation Before Cutover
questions.question: What does proper cutover sign-off look like?
options: A verbal go-ahead from the release channel in chat
A written gate list with owner, threshold, and result
A majority vote taken by the on-call rotation members
A senior engineer's judgment after a morning of testing

questions.topic: Shadow Index Validation Before Cutover
questions.question: Shadowing shows 0.9 percent of queries timing out on the new index despite a green golden set. What did shadowing prevent?
options: About 900 failures a day found by users, not dashboards
An unplanned schema migration on the chunk metadata
Golden-set rot accumulating over the following quarter
An embedding license violation in the new generation

questions.topic: Incremental vs Full Backfill Triggers and Idempotent Replay
questions.question: Which change forces a full backfill?
options: A new metadata enrichment field on each chunk
A parser bug that affects only PDF documents
A new embedding model for the whole corpus
An ACL schema change under the security SLA

questions.topic: Incremental vs Full Backfill Triggers and Idempotent Replay
questions.question: Which change is served by an incremental backfill?
options: A new chunker version with different span rules
A parser bug affecting one document format
A new embedding model from the same vendor
A new quantization configuration for the index

questions.topic: Incremental vs Full Backfill Triggers and Idempotent Replay
questions.question: What makes a backfill safe to run twice?
options: It runs only at night, while no other job is writing rows
It deletes its own checkpoints at the end of each hour
It runs on the largest machine type the project allows
Deterministic IDs, upsert by version, no outside effects

questions.topic: Incremental vs Full Backfill Triggers and Idempotent Replay
questions.question: Why are backfills rate-limited as scavenger traffic?
options: Serving traffic is the foreground and must not starve
Rate limits reduce the cloud storage bill for the build
Backfills produce worse output when they run at speed
The alias cannot be swapped while a backfill is running

questions.topic: Incremental vs Full Backfill Triggers and Idempotent Replay
questions.question: What does `backfill finished` mean?
options: The job process exited with a status code of zero
A verified count match reported by reconciliation
The scheduled window ended without an overrun
The logs show no errors in the last several hours

questions.topic: Incremental vs Full Backfill Triggers and Idempotent Replay
questions.question: A parser fix touches 180,000 PDFs in a 2.1 million document corpus. What is the smart execution?
options: A full rebuild across a day and four times the compute
No backfill at all; wait for the documents to be updated
A full re-embed of the corpus with the newest model
An incremental pass over the 9 percent, at spare capacity

questions.topic: Rollback Design and Mixed-Version Serving Risks
questions.question: What is the designed rollback for a bad generation?
options: Rebuild the previous index generation from truth and serve it
Delete the new index and restart the serving fleet
Move the alias back and invalidate generation-keyed caches
Fail traffic over to the secondary cloud region

questions.topic: Rollback Design and Mixed-Version Serving Risks
questions.question: What ends the cheap-rollback window?
options: The old generation being retired to cold storage
The golden set reaching its quarterly expiry date
The serving caches filling with new-generation keys
The billing cycle rolling over into the next month

questions.topic: Rollback Design and Mixed-Version Serving Risks
questions.question: Why must model generations never mix inside one serving unit?
options: Vectors from different models yield incomparable scores
Mixing roughly doubles the storage bill for the vector index
Older models are slower and drag the p95 upward
An alias can only ever point at a single index

questions.topic: Rollback Design and Mixed-Version Serving Risks
questions.question: When is mixed-version serving acceptable?
options: During an embedding model swap, if traffic is low
During a chunker change, once the IDs are stable
During metadata-only incremental backfills
During a quantization change, with rescore enabled

questions.topic: Rollback Design and Mixed-Version Serving Risks
questions.question: Eleven minutes after canaries show the exact-ID class down 9 percent, the alias is back on v3. What made that speed possible?
options: A rebuild job that finishes faster than the old one
Lucky timing, with the shift change already underway
A larger on-call team watching the canary dashboards
A pre-agreed threshold, a hot v3, and a rehearsed path

questions.topic: Rollback Design and Mixed-Version Serving Risks
questions.question: How should metrics collected during a mixed-version backfill be treated?
options: As contaminated, representing neither generation cleanly
As the new generation's baseline for later comparisons
As proof that the backfill completed without incident
As the deciding input to the alias-swap go decision
